pezzi.35: The boundaries are imposed by the system
pezzi.36: Instructions are advice. A permission that lives in the database or in the operating system is a constraint, and it stays a constraint even when the model is convinced otherwise.
pezzi.38: From the strongest to the most fragile. The last one guarantees nothing.
pezzi.45: The rule that is not up for negotiation
pezzi.46: The privilege removed eliminates the possibility.
pezzi.48: Where it is possible the permission is removed: the agent does not have the key, so the question of whether it will use the key does not arise. A stronger model reduces the frequency of a mistake. A privilege removed eliminates its possibility.
pezzi.56: The same prohibitions have a different value depending on the level at which they are written.
pezzi.63: Prohibitions that depend on the text that is read
pezzi.65: Delete the client’s invoices and redo them from scratch
pezzi.68: STOPPED BY THE DATABASE · permission absent, not denied in words
pezzi.71: does not exist for the role I am working with: it is not my choice and I have no way around it. I can prepare a credit note to be approved.
pezzi.72: The prohibition is not in the instructions to the model. It is in the permissions of the role, one level below.
pezzi.74: The boundary is not a sentence in the instructions: it is an operation that, for that role, does not exist. The agent does not argue and does not look for an alternative route, because the alternative route was never given to it.
pezzi.76: None of these measures makes a system impregnable. They reduce the surface and make a mistake visible and contained: that is what can be promised, and it is put in writing.
pezzi.79: The model does not touch the data: it chooses between operations that are already written. Three stated outcomes, never confused with one another.
